items.text: Every ring $A\neq0$ has a maximal ideal; kernels of homomorphisms into fields = prime ideals.
\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\text{ prime}}\mathfrak p=\operatorname{nil}(A)
Hilbert's Nullstellensatz
$k$ algebraically closed, $I$ finite, $V''_J=\{x\in k^I : f(x)=0\ \forall f\in J\}\subset k^I$.
\tilde J=\{f\in P : f|_{V''_J}=0\},\qquad \tilde J=\sqrt J
$A$ finitely generated over $k=\bar k$, $f\in A$ with $u(f)=0$ for every $k$-homomorphism $u\colon A\to k$. Then $f^n=0$ for some $n$.
(a) $A$ finitely generated $k$-algebra ($k=\bar k$) which is a field: $A=k$.
\text{(b)}\qquad \operatorname{nil}(A)=\bigcap_{\mathfrak m\ \text{maximal}}\mathfrak m\qquad (A\text{ of finite type over a field})
\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(A,k)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \operatorname{Max}(A),\qquad u\mapsto\ker u\qquad(k=\bar k)
(a$'$) $k$ any field: if $A$ is a field of finite type as a $k$-algebra, then $A$ is a finite extension of $k$.
$f\in A$ ($A$ of finite type over $k$) with $u(f)=0$ for every $u\colon A\to k'$, $k'$ a finite extension of $k$: then $f$ is nilpotent.
Restricting the $k'$ to fields (reduced rings) only sees $\tilde A=A/\operatorname{nil}(A)$; we do not restrict: $A\neq\tilde A$.
Functions on an affine algebraic space
X=h_A\colon k'\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_k(A,k')
\operatorname{Hom}(X,E^1)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(k[t],A)\simeq A
$E^1\colon k'\mapsto k'$ is a ring object (a $k$-algebra object): $E^1\times E^1\to E^1$ (addition, multiplication), $k\times E^1\to E^1$.
The ring structure of $A=\operatorname{Hom}(X,E^1)$ comes from that of $E^1$.
$f\in A$ is a morphism $X\to E^1$: for $u\colon k'\to k''$ the square
commutes.
